cards.front: What are the three categories of public communications under FINRA Rule 2210?
cards.back: 1) Institutional communications, 2) Retail communications, 3) Correspondence.

cards.front: Retail communication
cards.back: Any written (including electronic) communication distributed or made available to more than 25 retail investors within any 30-calendar-day period. Requires principal approval before use.

cards.front: Correspondence
cards.back: Any written (including electronic) communication distributed or made available to 25 or fewer retail investors within any 30-calendar-day period.

cards.front: Institutional communication
cards.back: Any written (including electronic) communication distributed only to institutional investors. Excludes internal communications. A retail investor is anyone other than an institutional investor.

cards.front: Which entities qualify as institutional investors for FINRA communication purposes?
cards.back: Another BD/RR, bank, S&L, insurance company, registered investment company, employee benefit plan, governmental entity, person acting on behalf of an institutional investor, and any entity (including natural persons) with $50 million or more in total assets.

cards.front: A firm sends a piece labeled 'institutional only' to a hedge fund, but knows the fund will share it with retail clients. How is the communication treated?
cards.back: It must be treated as a retail communication. A firm may not treat a piece as institutional if it has reason to believe any part will be forwarded to retail investors.

cards.front: Seacoast Securities is in its first year as a FINRA member and is launching a mass-mail retail advertisement. What is the filing requirement?
cards.back: New member firms (within the first year of FINRA membership) must file retail communications with FINRA at least 10 days BEFORE first use. Established firms file within 10 days OF first use.

cards.front: Does filing a retail communication with FINRA constitute regulatory approval?
cards.back: No. Filing is not an approval process — it is simply a filing requirement. Suggesting that FINRA or the SEC has approved a firm's communications or recommendations is misleading and prohibited.

cards.front: Under FINRA's social media rules, what is required for static content vs. interactive posts?
cards.back: Static content (websites, blogs) generally requires principal approval before use and may require FINRA filing. Interactive posts do not require pre-approval, but the firm must have written supervisory procedures covering these activities.

cards.front: What are the basic TCPA cold-calling rules?
cards.back: 1) Caller must identify name, firm name, and firm phone/address; 2) Calls only between 8:00 am and 9:00 pm in the prospect's time zone; 3) No calls to numbers on the firm's do-not-call list or the National Do Not Call Registry.

cards.front: Which calls are exempt from the TCPA?
cards.back: Calls to parties with an established business relationship or prior express permission; calls on behalf of tax-exempt nonprofits; non-commercial calls; and calls for legitimate debt collection.

cards.front: Before placing a cold call, which lists must a registered representative check, and how current must they be?
cards.back: Both the firm's internal do-not-call list AND the National Do Not Call Registry. Each list used must be no more than 30 days old.

cards.front: How often must customer account records be verified/updated under FINRA rules?
cards.back: A copy of the account record must be sent to the customer within 30 days of opening, within 30 days of any change, and at least every 36 months thereafter.

cards.front: How frequently must customer account statements be sent?
cards.back: At least quarterly. Monthly if there is activity in the account or if the account holds penny stocks.

cards.front: When must a trade confirmation be delivered to the customer?
cards.back: At or before the completion of the transaction (the settlement date).

cards.front: What capacity-related disclosure must appear on a trade confirmation?
cards.back: The capacity in which the BD acted — agent or principal. If acting as agent, the commission must be disclosed. If acting as principal, the markup/markdown replaces the commission line.

cards.front: What are the requirements for a firm to hold a customer's mail?
cards.back: 1) Written customer instructions specifying the time period (generally up to 3 months; longer for valid reasons like safety, not convenience); 2) Firm must inform customer of alternate ways to access account info and get confirmation that this was received; 3) Firm must verify at reasonable intervals that instructions still apply; 4) Firm must be able to communicate timely with the customer.

cards.front: Under Regulation SP, when must privacy notices be delivered to customers?
cards.back: At the time the customer relationship is established (initial notice) and annually thereafter. Consumers (one-time, limited relationships) receive only the initial notice.

cards.front: What opt-out methods are considered reasonable under Regulation SP for nonaffiliated third-party information sharing?
cards.back: Check-off form with prepaid return envelope, electronic opt-out (for customers who agreed to electronic delivery), or a toll-free phone number. Requiring the customer to write a letter is NOT reasonable.

cards.front: Under the 2024 amendments to Regulation S-P, within how many days must a firm notify customers of unauthorized access to sensitive customer information?
cards.back: Within 30 days. Firms must also maintain an incident-response program and expanded vendor oversight. Compliance dates: 12/3/2025 (large entities), 6/3/2026 (small entities).

cards.front: What must a FINRA member firm's Business Continuity Plan (BCP) address?
cards.back: Data backup/recovery, alternate communications with customers/employees/regulators, alternate physical locations, and prompt customer access to funds and securities if the firm cannot continue business.

cards.front: What are the requirements for FINRA emergency contact persons under the BCP rule?
cards.back: Firms must provide FINRA with two contacts — both must be associated persons, at least one must be a principal and part of senior management, and the second (if not a principal) must be part of senior management familiar with operations. Updates must be made promptly, no later than 30 days after any change.

cards.front: What are FINRA's general standards for ALL member communications with the public?
cards.back: Based on principles of fair dealing and good faith; clear and not misleading; fair and balanced as to risks and benefits; no omission of material facts; no false/exaggerated/misleading claims; no implication that past performance will recur; and tailored to the audience.

cards.front: What conditions must be met for a firm to deliver confirmations and statements electronically?
cards.back: The firm must have procedures showing delivery to the intended recipient, protect confidentiality and security of personal information, obtain the customer's written consent, and provide paper copies upon request.
